title: WPPIL/177/2019 of HEM KAPIL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (PIL) No.177 of 2019
Hem Kapil ..........Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and others ...........Respondents

Presents:-
Mr. D.N. Sharma, learned Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Amit Bhatt, learned Deputy Advocate General for the State of
Uttarakhand/respondent Nos.1 to 3.

Dated: 2nd November, 2019
Coram: Hon'ble Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.
 Hon'ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J. (Oral)

Admit.
2. The relief sought for in this Writ Petition is for a
mandamus directing the respondents to establish shelter
homes for stray dogs in Haldwani of District Nainital; a
mandamus directing the respondents to ensure mandatory
registration and license for keeping pet dog in Haldwani, and
the same be registered with the Nagar Nigam Haldwani.
3. Sri D.N. Sharma, learned counsel for the petitioner,
would draw our attention to the tabular statement, enclosed
along with the writ petition, which, according to him, reflects
the large sums of money available with the State Government
in its treasury at Haldwani. According to the learned counsel,
all these funds can be utilized for construction of shelter
homes for stray dogs. Matters for which the available funds
should be earmarked, and the projects for which these funds
should be utilized, are required to be examined by the
concerned officials, and this Court, in judicial review
proceedings under Article 226 of the Constitution of India,

2
would not issue a mandamus directing the State Government
to prioritize its expenditure in a particular manner.
3. While the petitioner's endeavor, to put an end to this
menace of motorcyclists being bitten by stray dogs is laudable,
we are satisfied that these are all matters for the authorities to
consider, and not for this Court to determine. Suffice it, in
such circumstances, to permit the petitioner to make a
representation to respondent Nos.2 and 5 highlighting all
these issues. Both respondent Nos.2 and 5 shall examine any
such representation made by the petitioner, and take
appropriate decisions, pursuant thereto, in accordance with
law.
4. The writ petition stands disposed of, accordingly. No
costs.
 (Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.)
 02.11.2019
Sanjay /NEHA
